boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Bean's Station record (December 14, 1863) in Longstreet's Knoxville Campaign [November-December 1863]. The December 15 fighting and pursuit toward Blain's Cross-Roads are outside the frozen interval; the live NPS page has no description, so the frozen description is cited. The siege, the November 23–25 actions, the pursuit and campaign-wide figures are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Cavalry Corps, Department of the Ohio, and the Confederate forces in East Tennessee without counts; the live field is blank. The frozen description says Shackelford had about 4,000 cavalry and infantry. Longstreet says he was told there were three brigades of cavalry and one of infantry at Bean's Station, and that his column was infantry and artillery only. Parke relays a prisoner's statement that Gracie's infantry brigade had the advance.
claims.rationale: No matched count is inspected; none is adopted. The live blank is not measured absence.

claims.value: Longstreet says Martin's cavalry crossed late and only in part, Jones retired from the gap, and that the next day Law's lateness, McLaws's unfed troops and a desire for rest made him abandon the pursuit, the second time in the campaign the enemy escaped. The frozen commanders are Lieutenant General Longstreet and Brigadier General Shackelford; the live heading ranks Longstreet Major General.
claims.rationale: Judgments are attributed; the pursuit decision falls after the frozen date. The frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. The frozen description says the Federals retired by nightfall toward Blain's Cross Roads; Parke reported that after dark Shackelford was compelled to fall back a short distance; Longstreet says his column could only drive the enemy back.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

open_questions: Shackelford's, Foster's and Kershaw's reports and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Burnside's, Parke's and Longstreet's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Burnside's full report was written in November 1865 and Longstreet's in January 1864. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
